description: A tape-style stereo delay with three heads at triplet, beat and dotted spacing, tape wear, and momentary freeze and bypass buttons

params.text: Sets the delay time up to 2 seconds; with a clock patched it instead picks a ratio of the clocked time from nine musical steps
Sets how much of the delayed signal returns to the delay line, topping out at 98%
Crossfades between the dry input and the delayed signal on an equal-power curve
Sets the tape saturation applied to the delayed signal, with make-up gain added over the top quarter of its travel
Adds tape wear: hiss builds over the lower half of its travel, then wow, flutter and volume dropouts over the upper half
Chooses one of six level balances for the three delay heads, named SUB, DUB, QTR, DOT, TRP and ALL from the bottom up; the lit squares printed beside the names do not match what it does
Multiplies the clocked delay time by a quarter, a half, one, two or four
Spreads the outer two heads apart by 0%, 15%, 35%, 60% or 90% of the delay time, pulling the triplet head earlier and the dotted head later
Widens the stereo image by reading the left channel earlier and the right channel later, by up to a quarter of the delay time
Held down, it freezes and blooms the echoes by lifting the feedback to at least 90% and adding drive; on release the freeze fades out over 3 seconds

Held down, it crossfades the output to the dry input over 1 second and back again on release; the delay keeps running underneath. The maker's manual calls this Break and describes a tape-stop slowdown

inputs.text: The left audio input, and the only signal that reaches the delay line
The right audio input; it is heard in the dry half of the mix only, and follows the left input when unpatched
Offsets TIME, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets FEEDBACK, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets MIX, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets DRIVE, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets TAPE, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Steps the HEADS selection, 2V per position
One pulse per quarter note, which sets the delay time together with DIVISION and TIME; pulses closer together than 0.1 seconds are ignored
Steps the OFFSET selection, 2.5V per position
Offsets SPREAD, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Freezes the echoes while the voltage here is above 1V, as holding SURGE down does
Crossfades the output to dry while the voltage here is above 1V, as holding DRY down does

outputs.text: The left output: dry and delayed signal at the balance set by MIX
The right output: dry and delayed signal at the balance set by MIX

notes: with nothing patched to CLOCK the delay runs free and TIME sets the time directly. With a clock patched, DIVISION and TIME are read as ratios of the measured beat
the delay line is mono and is fed from IN/L alone. IN/R reaches the output only through the dry half of the mix
menu: 1 PPQN (Submit standard) — reads each pulse at CLOCK as one quarter note
4 PPQN (compatibility) — reads four pulses at CLOCK as one quarter note
Clocked Time: Extra divisions — lets TIME choose a ratio of the clocked delay time from nine musical steps between a quarter and four; turned off, TIME does nothing while a clock is patched
